cells.remarks: Records the grant of some land in favour of Kavisūrya and others who were the sons of Jayadēva Mēdhi. It is stated that some land at Maṇuamāt-bīla was previously granted by the king Dhanyamāṇya on behalf of the king in favour of the Brāhmaṇa Jayadēva who was the Mēdhi of the satra at Silāgrāma in Bausi-pargaṇa and that he was deprived of the land fraudulently by Kavichūḍāmaṇi. The present grant was made in compensation for the land lost.

cells.date: Śaka 974, Nandana, Pauṣa śu. 15, total eclipse of the moon, Tuesday= 1052 A.D., December 8.
cells.remarks: Registers the king's grant of the four villages, vīz., Konurvī, Trayī, Pōyigatiã and Palasī-caturvëda-maṅgala, belonging to Brahmapura-Śrīdhara-daṇḍanayaka, whose great-grandfather Sīlana is said to have served Paramāra Vairisiṁha of Dhārā. The donee's family is stated to have hailed from Oyaṁgē-grāma in the Madhyadēśa. The grant was composed by the Kavaśa Taikatāyva, son of Vijayatya and was engraved by one Bhadra, son of Sōhanaya. Contains another record in continuation of the above, registering the grant of one village Dhalavātī and exchange for Kumarahara (?) by Sēūnacandra (II).

cells.location: Pulicat. Through Sri K. D. Swaminathan.
cells.place: Impressions and photographs from Sri Kamnappa Nacker, Panchayat Board President, Pulicat, Kalahasti Taluk.
cells.remarks: Registers the grant of four villages, viz., Chiṭṭūru, Māmbāka, agam and Puruvalupāka situated in Aṅsarvaka(Aṅcharapāka)-parru in Padaviṭu-sīma, by the king to the Brāhmaṇas, sons of Maṇidārya, and grandsons of Amuram Timmayya of the Ātrēya gōtra, Āśvalāyana sūtra and Ṛik śākhā. The four villages were constituted into one unit and renamed as Dattarājapura after the charter-granter, and one Chidambarakavi, the nephew of Śivasūrya, and was engraved by Kāmāchārya, son of Ganapaya and the younger brother of Vīraṇa.

cells.place: Śitalā temple, wall to the left of entrance.
cells.remarks: Records the erection, at Gayā, of a temple dedicated to various local deities, the digging of the Uttara-mānasā tank, and the establishment of a charitable hall by prince Yakṣapāla, son of king Viśvarūpa and grandson of king Śūdra-pāṇi. cells.location: Chikkerur
cells.place: Slab lying in front of the Panchayat office.
cells.date: Regnal year 4, Sun-mana, Uttarāyaṇa-saṅkrānti, solar eclipse. Irregular.
cells.remarks: Records a gift of 2 mattar of land for worship of and offerings to the god Chinnēśvara of the chin-neśi who had the temple also built; and also 2 mattar of land by the same donor towards the satra for Brāhmaṇas. The record contains an eulogy of the family and the family of a priest who was the mahājanas of the agrahāra of Chikkakereyūru. The composer of the record was Elegavi Tilaka-Paṇḍita and the engraver Kājoja.

cells.remarks: Records the installation of goddess Bhalāri by Pallijja, son of Dēvarāja-bhaṭṭa, of the family of Nījabhaṭṭa, and his wife Arasakka, when mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Āhava-malla had proceeded towards north against Utpala on a digvijaya after establishing peace in the hevva- 1000-viṣaya, then governing Banavāsi-1200 and Nāgārjjuna, was the nāl-gāmuṇḍa. Published in Ep. Ind., Vol. XXIII, pp. 131 ff.

cells.place: Slab lying in front of Kaḷlēśvara temple.
cells.date: Regnal year 7, Raktākshi, Āśvayuja Amāvāse, Monday. Irregular.
cells.remarks: Records gift of land to Mallikārjunapaṇḍita of the Lakuḷīśa sect by Tuyyala Begūra Kēṭagāvuṇḍa and others. It also states that Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Taila-Yōgēśvaradēva was governing Banavāsi-12000, from his capital at Baḷipura and Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Sōvidēva was governing Nāgarakhaṇḍa-70 from his capital at Baṇḍalike. The record contains a genealogical account of the family of the gāvuṇḍa of Tuyyala Bēgūru situated in Nāgarakhaṇḍa-70.

cells.place: Stone buried on the bund of tank called Duggavvana-kere.
cells.remarks: Records gift of income from the levy called hāgavana derived from the agrahāra triyākere, exempting the village, with the approval of the king, to the gods of other villages for the upkeep of the tank Heggere by Maṇḍalika Māsanarasa, Hemmaḍiyarasa of Raṭṭahaḷḷi, Sōmarasa, and the Śrīkaraṇa. cells.location: Satenahalli
cells.place: Slab fixed into the prākāra wall of Sāntēśa temple.
cells.date: Śaka 1501 (wrong for 1502), Vikrama, Māgha śu. 15, Friday, lunar eclipse= 1581 A.D., January 19, Thursday (not Monday).
cells.remarks: Records gift of the village Maddugoṇḍakoppa alias Hanumasamudra, for worship and offerings to god Hanumanta (of the temple at) Sātēnahalli by Laḍhe- nāyaka of Hāvasebhāvi who was agent of Sāḷu- vanna-nāyaka, the governor of Sāvanūru-sīme under the Kēḷadi, who was governing from Ikkēri. The gift was made at the instance of the latter for his welfare also that of Chinnappa-nāyaka, the father of the donor and also the mother. The village, which was situated to the south of Tījuvalli in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa sīme in Banavāsi-12000.

cells.place: Slab inside Nārāyaṇadēva temple.
cells.date: Year 31, Śarvari, Māgha śu. 10, Thursday=1241 A.D., January 24.
cells.remarks: Records the installation of the deity of Śaṁkarānārāyaṇadēva by nālprabhu Bommi-seṭṭi, son of Śaṁkara-seṭṭi. Further records gifts of land, garden and oilmill, the ownership of offerings for the god and for repairs etc. to the temple by the villagers and also by Bommi-seṭṭi, the former's mother Hanmmave and others. All these donors belonged to the Vīrabaṇañju community of Koṇavatti. The gift was made over to Kāṁchanna and three others belonging to Kaśyapa-gōtra.

cells.place: Do. No. 4
cells.date: Śaka 1312, Pramādi, Chaitra su. Friday = 1390 A.D., March, 18.
cells.remarks: Do. Records a grant of land, made probably by a subordinate (name lost) of the king, who is stated to have then camped at the capital of Honnāvāra. The gift-land which seems to have been given for a sarra was purchased from a person whose name also is lost. The land is situated at Bārakūru in Ālukhēḍa-nāḍu. The grant was made in the presence of the god Mahābala of Gōkarṇa.

cells.place: Slab built into the wall inside the temple of Vīrabhadra (to the left of Vīrabhadra shrine).
cells.date: Chālukya-Vikrama year 84, Pramādi, Śrāvaṇa ba. 5 Wednesday=1159 A. D., 15 August 5.
cells.remarks: Records the construction of the temples of Kamalaṇābha and Īśa by Chandrarāja and Āchirāja, sons of Cheṭṭa. Permanripāla is stated to be the governor of Keḷavāḍi, a subdivision of Eḍedore-nāḍu. Āchirāja was his subordinate officer in the administrative administration of the division. Tājikavāvi is highly praised.

cells.place: Same temple (to the left of Īśvara shrine).
cells.date: Year 8, Jaya, Bhādrapada ba. 15, Monday, solar eclipse. Irregular.
cells.remarks: Records the installation of Chandrēśvaraliṅga by Chandrarāja of the Taḷakāḍu family, situated in Keḷavāḍi, a subdivision of Eḍedore-nāḍu. Also records certain grants to the temple of the god Chandrēśvara. Keḷavāḍi was under the administrative control of Dūśira Kēśava-daṇḍanāyaka. Genealogy of Chandra is given. Tājikavāvi is described at length.

cells.date: Śaka 955, Śīmukha, Kārttika śu. 8, Thursday, Vi-shu-saṅkrānti= 1033 A.D., October 4. The saṅ-krānti occurred one September 26.
cells.remarks: Records a grant of money to Aṇṇanayya and the malajanas of agrahāra Taṇakavāvi situated in Keḷavāḍi-Three-hundred. The donors of the grant were Manevergade Chāvuṇḍamayya, Daṇḍanāyaka Kā-mayya and Kārdavayya. Another grant of money made by Māṇayya, Bāchasa of the Kaḍamba family is recorded. Bācharasa is called Banavāsi-puravarēśvara (lord of Banavāsi).

cells.place: Slab kept inside the Trya-mbakēśvara temple.
cells.date: Śaka 1140, current, Īśvara, Vaiśākha śu. 13, Thursday=1217 A.D., April 20, Thursday, f.d.t. 26.
cells.remarks: Enumerates the conquests of Singhaṇa. Gives an eulogistic account of Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Immaḍi Mallidēvarasa of the Ahihēya family and Bēchi-seṭṭi of Bēchi-seṭṭi the seṭṭiguttas of Moraṭa-300. Records the installation of a Śiva-liṅga and the gift in the name of their father. States that they also made a grant of land and money to Saṅkara-paṇḍita for the purpose of worshipping the god Tryambakēśvara.

cells.location: Unchahra, Nagod Tahsil, Satna District.
cells.place: Fifth pillar.
cells.remarks: Fragmentary. Records the construction of a temple for the god Vāmana-svāmin by the Gāhaḍavāla king, son of Mahārājādhirāja Bhārathadeva of the Rāshṭra (Rāshṭrakūṭa) family of Kanyakubjādeśa and chief queen of Mahāmandadeva who was a subordinate of the king. Also mentions a ruler called Rājyade-chaka-deva. Lakshmaṇa-deva or Dharmadeva who was related to Uddaladevī on the mother's side. Composed by Paṇḍita Sukhākara. Paṇḍita Śasyakara seems to have written the letters on the stone for the work of the clerk of the engraver. Published in Ep. Ind., Vol. XXXIII, pp. 121 ff.

cells.place: Findspot : Pehoa, Karnal District.
cells.remarks: Records the building of a triple temple of Vishṇu by Gōgga, Pūrṇarāja and Dēvarāja belonging to the Tōmara family and assigns them to the Yāśōvarmmapura, Tōlaka, Gējjaṛa and Pātāla for the bhōga of the deity. Achyuta, son of Rāma, was the architect. The composer of the praśasti whose name is lost was the son of Bhaṭṭa Rāma and the engraver was [ā]ditya, son of Dhaṇṇabhadra. In characters of the 9th-10th century A. D. Published in Ep. Ind., Vol. I, pp. 242 ff. and Plate.

cells.place: BENGAL, WEST CALCUTTA Cast of a coin in the Indian Museum, Calcutta.
cells.remarks: Silver, round. Wt. 164 grs. S. 9 in. Obv. In a lined square, 5 lines of legend: Ma-hārāja-śrī-Da-[rppa]ṇḍa-yan-ātma-ja; in four interspaces outside the square but within a lined circle surrounded by a wavy line, [śa] in upper l., [ka] in upper r., [1] in upper l., [4] in lower r., [1] in lower l., [1] in lower r. Letters rā and ya of Nārāyaṇa are damaged by later punchings by shroffs. Rev. In lined square, 5 lines of legend: Tr[rabhuk]t-rā-śrī-Bhaira-lvas[m]ha-isya; in four interspaces o-tside the square but within a lined circle surrounded by a wavy line, [ra] in upper l., [jya] in upper r., [1] in lower l., [4] in lower r., [1] in lower r. (The date and regnal year and numerals are cut off in this coin but are almost intact on coin No. 2 below). The letter ra of Tira-bhukti is damaged by later punching by shroffs. See Ep. Ind., Vol. XXXII, p. 353, Postscript. Smith, I. M. Cat., I, p. 353, No. ?

cells.place: BIHAR MONGHYR DISTRICT Cast of a coin from Prof. R.K. Chow-dhary, G.D. College, Begusarai.
cells.remarks: Silver, round. Wt. 162-37 grs. S. 1 in. Obv. and Rev. As No. 1 above, but being struck with a different die and being slightly larger than that of the above coin, the letters and numerical figures both on the obverse and reverse exergue are almost intact. In some cases, forms of letters (e.g. ha in mahārāja) are similar and different; and as on No. 1, the letters da, rppa and ṇa on the obverse, and ja and śrī on the reverse are damaged by later punchings by shroffs. Published in Ep. Ind., Vol. XXXII, pp. 327 ff. and Plate; see also JNSI, Vol. XX, pp. 57 ff. This coin is published as an issue of King Rāmabhadra.

cells.place: Casts of coins from the Prince of Wales Museum of Western India, Bombay.
cells.remarks: Gold, round. S. about 1·5 centimeter each. Obv. In a lined circle with a row of dots around, the figure of a fully armed warrior running to left against decorations that have the shape of a dagger pointed to the front and in the left, a hawk with outspread wings facing the warrior; the symbol of the sun is in front of the warrior and that of the moon, behind him. Rev. In a lined circle with a row of dots, a legend in 3 lines: Śrī-Nigala-/[m]kamala-Da(ṇ)i-(d)inag(a)va. Weights: No. 3—60 grs., No. 4—59·75 grs., No. 5 —59·75 grs., No. 6—59·75 grs., No. 7—59·75 grs., No. 8—59·5 grs. and No. 9—60 grs. See Ep. Ind., Vol. XXXIII, p. 77, Plate, Coins 1 and 4 to 9.
